diagnostic_evidence.quote:
R_\theta(D_k)
=
\int_{\partial D_k}
\left(
U_\theta\, n_t + F(U_\theta)\cdot n_x
\right)\, dS.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims prescribed boundary conditions are enforced automatically when a control-volume face lies on the physical boundary. But R_\theta(D_k) evaluates the flux at the network's own trace U_\theta; no prescribed boundary datum appears in the residual or anywhere in the total loss (initial data enter only via the temporal ansatz at t=0). For hyperbolic conservation laws, boundary conditions must be imposed weakly through the boundary flux using prescribed exterior states (inflow/upwind fluxes); integrating F(U_\theta)\cdot n_x over a boundary face only enforces flux balance of whatever values the network happens to take there and constrains nothing. The claim is false as written.

failure_location.quote: When a boundary face of a control volume $D_k$ coincides with the physical boundary of the domain $\Omega_x$, the flux integration across this face directly enforces the prescribed boundary conditions naturally through the evaluation of $R_\theta(D_k)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete or qualify the claim (boundary faces merely contribute the network's own flux to the balance), or add explicit boundary-data terms, e.g. prescribed-state fluxes on faces lying on the physical boundary.
issues.overall_effect: As described, the method imposes no boundary conditions at all; none of the numerical sections specify boundary data, and the convergence framework (test functions compactly supported in space--time) is silent about boundaries. The advertised seamless boundary enforcement does not exist.
issues.title: Boundary conditions claimed to be enforced by flux evaluation alone
issues.why_classification: No formal result depends on the claim (the theory uses compactly supported test functions); removing the sentence or adding standard weak boundary fluxes is a local change that leaves the method, the theory, and the advertised scope intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The TVD regularization guarantees $\sup_{t \in [0,T]} TV(U_\theta(\cdot, t)) \leq M$ for some constant $M$;

issues.failure_explanation: Adding L_TVD as a soft term in a weighted-sum objective and minimizing it does not imply any a priori inequality sup_t TV(U_\theta) <= M: a penalty is not a constraint, and smallness of the total loss yields no hard bound on any one term. Additionally, the implemented estimator takes a maximum over finitely many random times and a sum over finitely many random points, which underestimates the true supremum over [0,T] and can miss oscillations between samples, so even the penalized quantity is only a lower approximation of sup_t TV. Theorem thm:added-2 properly lists the bound as an assumption; the defect is the prose assertion that the method guarantees it.

failure_location.quote: To guarantee this condition, we introduce a TVD regularization term:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword: the TVD term promotes bounded variation, and the uniform bound is an assumption to be verified a posteriori (or enforced via a hard constraint/projection). The conditional theorem is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Applicability of the main convergence theorem to the trained network rests on hypothesis 2, which the method is claimed but not shown to deliver; nothing in the paper establishes sup_t TV(U_\theta) <= M.
issues.title: TVD penalty asserted to guarantee a uniform total-variation bound
issues.why_classification: The theorem states the TV bound as an explicit hypothesis, so the formal implication survives; the repair is a wording correction or an a posteriori check with no loss of mathematical content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Applying the divergence theorem on each $D_i$, the continuous residual translates into boundary flux integrals, corresponding exactly to the local conservation residual $R_{\mathrm{cons}}(D_i)$ and entropy residual $R_{\mathrm{ent}}(D_i, k)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed control of the Kruzhkov-type dual defect E_R by the residuals of one fixed partition is impossible. Counterexample within the paper's own definitions (Burgers flux f(u)=u^2/2, entropy pair (u^2/2, u^3/3)): take any partition, a smooth w not identically zero compactly supported in the interior of a single cell D_j, and U_\theta = (t/T)\,\varepsilon w (which satisfies the temporal ansatz with U_0 = 0). Then U_\theta vanishes on every cell boundary, so R_\theta(D_i) = 0 and E_\theta(D_i) = 0 for all i, hence L_cons = L_ent = 0; but for k=0 and a test function \varphi \in \mathcal{A} with \partial_t\varphi \approx 1 on supp w, \mathcal{R}_{0,\varphi}(U_\theta) = \varepsilon\int |w|\,\partial_t\varphi + O(\varepsilon^2) > 0, so E_R(U_\theta) > 0 while the stated right-hand side is 0. The proof's steps are also invalid as written: integration by parts yields boundary integrals weighted by \varphi itself (plus interior strong-residual terms \int_{D_i}\varphi\,\mathrm{sgn}(U_\theta-k)(\partial_t U_\theta+\nabla\cdot F)), from which the factor (||\partial_t\varphi||_\infty+||\nabla\varphi||_\infty) cannot be factored to obtain the unweighted residuals; the object R_ent(D_i,k) is never defined; and the one-sided loss built from a single entropy pair cannot bound the supremum over the whole Kruzhkov family |\cdot-k|. Root cause: cell residuals over one fixed partition probe only piecewise-constant test fields and cannot control the W^{1,\infty}-test-function supremum without refinement-dependent consistency terms.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must restate the link over a refining or dense family of control volumes (maximal diameter h tending to 0, N_D tending to infinity), add a space--time BV (or equivalent oscillation) bound on U_\theta, control the full Kruzhkov entropy family (or prove that the single strictly convex entropy loss controls it in the scalar case), and prove a test-function approximation lemma. The resulting bound necessarily contains additional h-dependent consistency terms, so convergence holds only in the joint limit of vanishing losses and refining volumes, and the stated quarter-rate in terms of the two losses alone must be withdrawn.
issues.overall_effect: The main convergence theorem loses its only link between the training losses and E_R (Step 3 quotes the lemma verbatim); the quarter-rate L^1 bound and the convergence corollary are unproven, and the abstract/introduction claims of a rigorous convergence analysis and the first explicit L^1 convergence rate for a mesh-free control-volume PINN become unreliable. Separately, the lemma is stated for partitions while the algorithm evaluates the loss on randomly sampled, non-covering, multi-scale volumes, so even a repaired partition lemma would not directly apply to the implemented loss.
issues.title: Lemma bounding the weak truncation error by the discrete losses is false
issues.why_classification: The lemma is false as stated (explicit counterexample with exactly zero losses but positive defect) and it is the paper's central theoretical contribution; every correct replacement requires new hypotheses and a new approximation argument, and changes the advertised guarantee, since small losses at fixed sampling no longer imply small L^1 error. The main theorem and the headline rate claim do not survive as stated.

issues.failure_explanation: Because the Section-3 losses carry the factor 1/N_D, the identity is \sum_i \|R(D_i)\|^2/|D_i| = N_D \, L_{\mathrm{cons}}(\theta) (and similarly for the entropy term). The Cauchy--Schwarz step therefore yields \sum_i |R(D_i)| \le \sqrt{N_D\,|\Omega\times(0,T)|}\,\sqrt{L_{\mathrm{cons}}}, so the lemma's stated constant \sqrt{|\Omega\times(0,T)|} is too small by a factor \sqrt{N_D} whenever N_D > 1; the proof establishes only the weaker bound containing \sqrt{N_D}. This normalization slip is independent of the structural falsity in ISSUE-003. The main theorem's constant K_opt correspondingly misses a factor N_D^{1/4}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor \sqrt{N_D} in the lemma's bound and N_D^{1/4} in K_opt (or drop the 1/N_D normalization in the loss definitions); a forced, local correction. Note that any refinement-based repair of ISSUE-003 must additionally avoid constants that grow with N_D.
issues.overall_effect: The stated constants in Lemma 1 and in Theorem thm:added-2 are wrong by factors \sqrt{N_D} and N_D^{1/4} respectively; for fixed N_D the convergence statement itself (losses tending to 0) is unaffected.
issues.title: Missing sqrt(N_D) normalization factor in the loss-based bound
issues.why_classification: A single forced algebraic correction restores the intended inequality with no change to the method, the rate, or the convergence claim at fixed N_D; no new argument or loss of content.

issues.failure_explanation: Asserting that the rate 1/4 is optimal requires lower-bound or saturation examples showing the estimate chain is sharp; no such argument appears anywhere in the paper. The exponent is simply the outcome of composing a square-root (Bouchut--Perthame) estimate with another square root (Lemma 1), and the sharpness of neither step is discussed. Moreover the rate itself rests on the defective Lemma 1 (ISSUE-003). The claim is unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: The convergence rate of $1/4$ is optimal for arbitrary control volume partitions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the word optimal or replace the sentence by the supported statement that the analysis yields a rate of 1/4, unless a saturating worst-case example is supplied.
issues.overall_effect: Overstates the strength of the convergence result; readers are led to believe the quarter rate cannot be improved within the framework, which the paper does not establish.
issues.title: Unsupported optimality claim for the 1/4 convergence rate
issues.why_classification: A local wording correction removes the unsupported sharpness assertion; no other claim or proof depends on optimality.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This construction guarantees $U_\theta(x,0) \equiv U_0(x)$, eliminating the initial condition error term from the convergence analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: The temporal ansatz makes U_\theta(x,0) = U_0(x) an identity, so every relative error at t=0 must vanish identically (the two functions compared are literally equal, independent of quadrature). Yet the error tables report nonzero WE-PINNs errors in the t=0.0 column: 8.07e-03 (L1) for the Riemann shock, and likewise 1.702e-03 (rarefaction), 1.824e-02 (interaction), 1.776e-03 and 4.787e-02 (dam-break). Either the ansatz was not used in the reported runs or the errors were computed or reported inconsistently; the source does not reconcile the contradiction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute or correct the t=0 entries (which must be zero under the ansatz), or state explicitly that the reported solutions were trained or evaluated without the temporal ansatz.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed exact enforcement of the initial condition and the reported initial-time accuracy cannot both hold; the evaluation protocol behind all the error tables is cast into doubt.
issues.title: Nonzero reported errors at t=0 contradict the exact-initial-condition ansatz
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the reported numbers or a clarifying sentence resolves the inconsistency; the method, the theory, and the other numerical claims are untouched.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In all cases, the entropy functions are convex and the corresponding entropy fluxes satisfy the compatibility condition with the physical flux, ensuring consistency with the entropy inequality.

issues.failure_explanation: For the 1D shallow-water system in conserved variables (h, hu), eta = (1/2)hu^2 + (1/2)gh^2 gives grad(eta) = (gh - u^2/2, u) and DF = [[0,1],[gh - u^2, 2u]], so compatibility requires grad(q) = (u(gh - u^2), gh + 3u^2/2), i.e. q = (1/2)hu^3 + gh^2 u = (eta + (1/2)gh^2)u. The stated flux q = eta*u = (1/2)hu^3 + (1/2)gh^2 u has half the required barotropic term and fails the compatibility relation (the same defect occurs componentwise in 2D). Consequently, for smooth exact solutions the quantity penalized by L_ent satisfies the boundary integral of (eta n_t + (eta u).n_x) equals minus the integral of partial_x((1/2) g h^2 u), which is nonzero in general and can be positive, so the SWE entropy residual is not entropy production and even penalizes the exact smooth solution. The closing claim of Appendix C that the pairs satisfy the compatibility condition is false for the shallow-water pair.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace q by (eta + (1/2) g h^2) u (componentwise in the multi-dimensional case); the correction is forced by the compatibility equations. The shallow-water numerical results should be recomputed with the corrected pair for the entropy-enforcement claims to hold as described.
issues.overall_effect: The entropy inequality enforced in the shallow-water experiments (1D dam break and the 2D SWE appendix tests) is the wrong inequality; entropy-admissibility enforcement for SWE is inconsistent with the paper's own compatibility requirement. The scalar convergence theory, which uses the Kruzhkov family, is unaffected.
issues.title: Shallow-water entropy flux violates the stated compatibility condition
issues.why_classification: The repair is a forced, one-term coefficient correction localized to the SWE entropy pair; no formal result depends on it (the theory is restricted to scalar laws), and the method and advertised scope survive unchanged.
